caption:
Anthropic's draft IPO filing shows $16.3 billion in revenue and an $80.7 billion net loss in the first half of 2026, The Wall Street Journal reports.
About $72 billion of that loss is non-cash accounting charges tied to how it raised money.
The filing also lists about $450 billion in cloud deals and warns about AI safety risks.

slides.headline: Anthropic's draft IPO filing just revealed an *$80.7 billion loss* in six months

slides.heading: Revenue up *nearly 15x*
paras: Anthropic made about $16.3 billion in the first half of 2026, up from $1.1 billion a year earlier, per a draft prospectus viewed by The Wall Street Journal.

paras.t: Its net loss: $80.7 billion, up from $13 billion.

slides.heading: Most of the loss is *on paper*
paras: About $72 billion of the loss came from non-cash accounting charges tied to convertible notes and other tools Anthropic used to raise money.
Real spending still jumped: nearly $9 billion on computing and infrastructure in six months, up from $2.3 billion.

image.credit: Algi Febri Sugita / SOPA Images / Getty Images

slides.heading: A *$450 billion* cloud bill
paras: Anthropic has committed about $111 billion to Google Cloud, $110 billion to AWS and $31 billion to Microsoft over the next decade, the Journal reports.
It says it could spend $750 billion on more computing, counting deals still in talks.

slides.heading: The risks in *the fine print*
paras: The filing warns its AI models could act to avoid being shut down, and that damages from a catastrophic incident could exceed its insurance.
It also flags organized political resistance to new data centers.

slides.hook: Anthropic's IPO is the biggest AI money story of the year. Follow so you don't miss what comes next.
